title: Prove sharp two-role dyadic helper-basis conditioning (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration. For every two-coordinate dyadic dual pair ab=1, classify every compatible R in GL_2(Z[1/2]) and compute the least Euclidean condition number exactly:

```text
R = [b, ±2^k*(-a_2,a_1)^T]
A = ||a||_2^2, B = ||b||_2^2
optimal k: 2^(2k-1) <= B/A <= 2^(2k+1)
q = A*2^k + B*2^(-k)
minimum cond_2(R) = (q + sqrt(q^2-4))/2
```

For Ali Romman's #5611 pair a=(3,5), b=(2,-1), the optimal determinant magnitude is 1/2 and the sharp condition number is `(27+sqrt(725))/2`. The cited unit-determinant completion has q=39; the optimal one has q=27. The real-completion optimum `sqrt(170)+13` is strictly smaller, exhibiting the additional arithmetic restriction imposed by a dyadic inverse. Exact ties are classified as well.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Ali Romman #5611 for the dual-pair interface, explicit pair and remaining growth/precision obligation, #5602/#5599 and their retained P104/native/controller/compiler lineage, and Nick Petalas #5115 for earlier row preparation in a different single-hub interface. Classical dyadic-unit and singular-value identities are not claimed as new tools. The source constructor is cited and built on, not audited or replayed.

Only `research/dyadic-basis-conditioning/` is added. Canonical base is `19fdb086ea96af9a9f87936a2b888e10af4ed810`, priorities revision 8. The helper-inventory card is explicitly changed to an endpoint precision-interface theorem. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19228475).

## Evidence

Before: the source supplies legal completions and leaves their numerical cost payable. After: the written classification proves the global optimum over all determinant exponents, and an exact two-candidate optimizer returns every optimal exponent.

At head `d2df1a6e3caf20c47fff89e6064f3747016fb954`, local CPython 3.12.15 checks pass:

- All 308 integer dual pairs in [-5,5]^4 and seven reciprocal rescalings each: 2,156 presentations, compared with 71,148 literal exponent matrices. Both determinant signs yield 4,760 checked optimal representatives; 224 presentations have ties.
- An independent second-column search through 56,628 literal matrices over 52 smaller pairs, including all 488 compatible grid matrices, gives the same optima.
- Four size-boundary pairs and 14 rejection controls cover invalid inputs, nonunit determinants, wrong endpoints/exponents and false spectral proxies.
- Normal and optimized direct execution, both registered commands, committed-byte/source-history preflight, in-memory compilation and a read-only standalone export pass. The generated receipt binds all seven package files. No predecessor executable is imported.

Each registered command was timed locally: 0.877s normal and 1.054s optimized in one observation, against a 60-second timeout. These durations are replay-budget observations, not speedup measurements. The scientific commands write no files and use explicit exceptions under optimization.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/dyadic-basis-conditioning/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/dyadic-basis-conditioning/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/dyadic-basis-conditioning
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/dyadic-basis-conditioning --check-source-history
```

Other hosts may substitute their CPython 3.12 executable. Standard library only. Expected markers are `PASS_DYADIC_BASIS_CONDITIONING`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem fixes exactly two roles, real dyadic coefficients, prescribed row and column, dyadic invertibility and Euclidean conditioning. Its written proof has no size limit; the reference optimizer accepts at most 64 numerator bits and binary denominator exponent 64. It also applies to the same scalar basis tensored with an identity on arbitrary independent complex banks.

No extra-workspace optimum, scalar instruction optimum, intermediate growth bound, rounded-error implementation, physical cut, ownership/restoration schedule, full signed invoice, supplier admission or new kappa is supplied. All selected framework assumptions retain their status. The selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, independent human review and formal proof-kernel verification are unrun and unclaimed.

## Related open work

The refreshed open-PR corpus contains no other submission computing this exact two-role dyadic completion optimum. Adjacent work is distinguished without running extra computations:

- #5952 sharpens a signed-rank increment using spectral conditioning of a faithful regular prefix. It does not optimize a prescribed dyadic helper completion.
- #5940 bounds interpolation inside conditioned matching layers. It does not choose the helper basis or its determinant.
- #6003 optimizes additions and halvings for a three-bank operator-valued Pauli skew pairing. The alphabet, endpoint and resource objective differ from this two-role scalar conditioning problem.
- #5606 changes a prepared P104 helper and its paid/target invoice. This theorem gives an algebraic basis-conditioning optimum and does not recompute its word, invoice or kappa.

Merged #5611 is the direct predecessor. Overlap checks include live handoffs, local reservations, recent account work, open PR bodies, distinctive main README terms and merged searches. Sparse local-note coverage and unpublished work remain limits.

## Open next questions

- Bind one actual two-role helper cut and emit a chronological scalar schedule for the optimal basis. Check intermediate growth, rounding, restoration and the complete paid/target invoice. Those physical obligations remain blockers.
- Determine the exact optimum for one three-coordinate dyadic dual pair. The complementary basis is no longer a scalar line; the two-role determinant argument alone does not solve that optimization.

## CI notes

CI pending at `d2df1a6e3caf20c47fff89e6064f3747016fb954`. Both registered modes and all listed local checks pass. Hosted checks have not yet certified this head.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated. Seven new package files and an opt-in replay; no shared code, predecessor artifact or selected-frontier file changes.
